-87.82420,42.10290.name: Davies Fertility & IVF Specialists, SC
-87.82420,42.10290.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Susan A. Davies, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-121.65450,37.13041.name: Aragen Bioscience, Inc.
-121.65450,37.13041.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Aragen. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.30219,51.72489.name: CREATE Fertility Hertfordshire
-0.30219,51.72489.state: CREATE Fertility, Colney Medical Centre, 45-47 Kings Road, St Albans, Hertfordshire, AL2 1ES
-0.30219,51.72489.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, London St Paul's
-0.30219,51.72489.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, London St Paul's. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-79.18450,43.81962.name: Toronto Zoo
-79.18450,43.81962.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, January 2024
-79.18450,43.81962.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, January 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-70.30500,43.69000.name: EnviroLogix — QuickStix strip tests
-70.30500,43.69000.desc: The strips most widely used at grain elevators, sold to anyone in packs of twenty-five or fifty at a few pounds each. Crush tissue or seed in water, dip the strip, read it in five to ten minutes. Strips are trait-specific: the common ones are CP4 EPSPS for glyphosate tolerance and the Bt proteins Cry1Ab, Cry1F and Cry1Ac. Combs testing several traits at once cost a little more. It finds a protein, so it cannot find a gene-edited organism, which usually has no novel protein for a strip to bind, and it will not work on cooked or refined material.
